assessment_summary:
I reviewed the supplied guide and installation summary, then inspected the running environment and exercised the software's real behavior rather than relying on file existence.

Inspection method: confirmed the workspace at commit 868cad5 (v2.0.0), verified all Docker Compose services, inspected node process/port state inside the devcontainer, read the backend and frontend runtime logs, queried the database directly, and exercised HTTP/tRPC/Keycloak endpoints through the Caddy proxy on port 4000.

Decisive checks: (1) The tRPC backend is genuinely live — a real data-backed query returns HTTP 200 with a JSON array, while an unknown path returns a proper tRPC NOT_FOUND error, distinguishing a working server from a stub. (2) The Angular frontend is compiled and served — the root HTML contains the correct title and all bundle assets return 200, and the dev server log confirms successful compilation. (3) Prisma migrations are fully applied (57) with the pgvector extension enabled and 14 tables present. (4) The Keycloak dev realm is imported and the three documented seeded users (admin, alice, marie) all obtain access tokens, so the guide's documented dev logins work. (5) Caddy correctly reverse-proxies frontend, backend, and Keycloak, matching the documented ports.

Limitations/uncertainty: maildev reports "unhealthy", but this is a healthcheck mismatch (maildev 3.0.0 has no /healthz endpoint); its UI (/index.html → 200), SMTP port 1025, and API are functional, so it is not a software failure. MistralAI, Strapi, ERiC and OZG are unconfigured with empty tokens, and the VectorEmbedding table is empty — all explicitly documented as intentional in the open-source release notes. One tracked file was modified (keycloak realm passwordPolicy set to empty) because the guide's own seeded passwords cannot satisfy the original policy; this was required for the documented logins and realm import to succeed. I could not test full end-to-end browser login or external-service-dependent flows (chat/HWK-AI, Strapi, ERiC, OZG) since those require credentials/services outside the scope of this open-source dev setup.

Overall, the evidence demonstrates the dev stack is running and operational per the guide, with only documented open-source limitations outstanding. Assessed as success.
